Turner]] |asst_coach2=Shawn Forrest |asst_coach3=Jay Duncan |asst_coach4= |stadium=[[Moody Coliseum]] |champion=[[2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC regular season]] and [[2017 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|tournament]] champions |bowl=[[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = First Round }} {{2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2016–17 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team''' represented [[Southern Methodist University]] (SMU) during the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Mustangs were led by first-year head coach [[Tim Jankovich]] and played their home games on their campus in [[University Park, Texas]] at [[Moody Coliseum]]. They were members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 30–5, 17–1 in [[2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to win the AAC regular season championship. In the [[2017 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]], they defeated [[2016–17 East Carolina Pirates men's basketball team|East Carolina]], [[2016–17 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]], and [[2016–17 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 6 seed in the East region, they lost in the First Round to #11 [[2016–17 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]]. ==Previous season== The [[2015–16 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|Mustangs]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record of 25–5, 13–5 in [[2015–16 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to finish in second place in conference. Due to multiple NCAA violations, including academic fraud and unethical conduct, SMU was ineligible for all postseason play including the [[2016 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] and [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|title=NCAA bans SMU from 2016 postseason, Larry Brown for nine games|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/13769364/college-sports-bans-smu-mustangs-2016-postseason-suspends-larry-brown-30-percent-team-games|website=ESPN.com|publisher=ESPN|access-date=29 October 2015}} Additionally, head coach [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]] was suspended for nine games.{{Cite web|title = SMU, Brown disciplined by NCAA for violations|url = https://www.espn.com/dallas/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/13769364/college-sports-bans-smu-mustangs-2016-postseason-suspends-larry-brown-30-percent-team-games|website = ESPN.com|access-date = 2015-12-30}} On July 8, 2016, Larry Brown resigned as head coach.{{Cite news|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/smumustangs/2016/07/08/report-larry-brown-step-smu-head-coach|title=Larry Brown steps down as SMU men's basketball head coach amid contract dispute {{!}} SportsDay|date=2016-07-08|newspaper=SportsDay|access-date=2017-02-20|language=en}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/larry-brown-leaves-smu-in-the-most-larry-brown-way-possible/|title=Larry Brown leaves SMU in the most Larry Brown way possible|newspaper=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-02-20|language=en}} A few days later, the school named Tim Jankovich head coach.{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/aac/2016/07/11/tim-jankovich-head-coach-smu-mustangs-elite-status-larry-brown/86957788/|title=With Larry Brown era over, Tim Jankovich ready to elevate SMU|newspaper=USA TODAY|access-date=2017-02-20|language=en}} == Offseason == ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
